title: English Elm: Ancient English Elms You Can Visit
meta_description: Dutch elm disease erased it across England. Brighton's Preston Twin, planted around 1613, is the city's survivor, 6.38 metres round.
intro: Dutch elm disease took the mature English elm almost everywhere in England, so most of the old ones now stand somewhere else. Brighton is the exception: it has cut infected wood out of its elms since the early 1970s, and the surviving Preston Twin, planted around 1613 in what was probably a hedgerow, is 6.38 metres round; its felled twin was carved and raised again on the same ground. Melbourne kept its elms too. In Boston, Saint-Gaudens built his memorial to Robert Gould Shaw and the Massachusetts 54th around a pair planted between 1772 and 1812, on a vault designed to spare their roots. New York's Hangman's Elm on Washington Square is put at 300 years or more, with a nickname no court or newspaper record supports. Portland's was the only elm left on its block after the Columbus Day Storm of 1962.
